evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.39.2: suffugium nūllum aut imbris aut sōlis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A place one runs under for cover: post-Augustan (Seneca, Pliny, Tacitus). Also, figuratively, a remedy or way out.

terms.gloss: a refuge, a place to flee to
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.150: perfugium omnium labōrum et sollicitūdinum somnus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Refuge from danger or trouble, a safe haven; the classical word of Plautus, Caesar and Cicero.

terms.gloss: a roof; a roof over one’s head
terms.comment: Shelter as a building: tēctō recipere (Cic.), to give someone shelter; sub tēctum, under cover (see roof). The ē is long by Lachmann’s law (tegō).

phrases.latin: nec aliud īnfantibus ferārum imbriumque suffugium quam ut in aliquō rāmōrum nexū contegantur
phrases.english: their babies have no other shelter from wild beasts and rain than to be covered over in a tangle of branches
It’s raining: let’s take shelter under the porch.
